metadata.title: Trusted foundry & secure microelectronics: the hardware root under PQC

notes: Ported/condensed from bubble-map trusted-foundry spec. Why it belongs here: PQC roots-of-trust (key storage, secure boot, HSMs) must be fabricated in trusted facilities - hardware assurance underpins the whole PQC migration, and leading-edge fab is a single-point geopolitical chokepoint (TSMC/Taiwan).

entities.name: Trusted_Foundry
entities.notes: DoD program (run by DMEA/TAPO since 2003, moved from NSA in 2015) guaranteeing US-government access to trusted microelectronics for typically low-volume defense needs; accredits the whole chain - design, mask, fab, packaging, test.

entities.name: DMEA_TAPO
entities.notes: Defense Microelectronics Activity / Trusted Access Program Office. Administers Trusted Foundry accreditation. NSA->defense microelectronics lineage. Trusted Foundry Access III ~$576M ceiling (DMEA 2026).

entities.name: RAMP_C
entities.notes: Rapid Assured Microelectronics Prototypes - Commercial. Awarded via the S2MARTS OTA. Gives DoD domestic LEADING-EDGE prototypes (answering the TSMC/Taiwan dependency). Intel completed it on 18A (RibbonFET+PowerVia).

entities.name: SHIP_Packaging
entities.notes: State-of-the-art Heterogeneous Integrated Packaging. DoD access to advanced 2.5D/3D packaging + chiplets - the other half of trusted assurance beyond the fab.

entities.name: Secure_Enclave
entities.notes: Program funding a dedicated, walled leading-edge Intel manufacturing capability for DoD (successor focus after RAMP-C) - onshore assured supply of advanced nodes. 'Trusted enclave in a commercial fab' model.

entities.name: SkyWater
entities.notes: SkyWater Technology (Bloomington MN). US-owned DMEA-accredited/DoD trusted foundry - the domestic trusted-but-not-leading-edge tier (trailing-edge + specialty).

entities.name: IBM
entities.notes: Holds DMEA Trusted Supplier accreditation; Trusted Foundry Access II establishes secured flows + embedded security at commercial advanced fabs. IBM-microelectronics lineage recurs (GlobalFoundries, Rapidus 2nm).

entities.name: BAE_Systems
entities.notes: BAE Microelectronics Center (Nashua NH) - long-standing trusted/rad-hard foundry for defense. The prime-owned trusted-fab model.

entities.name: Rapidus
entities.notes: METI-backed, Hokkaido. Targets 2nm using licensed IBM nanosheet technology - Japan's allied leading-edge onshoring bet (yield/timeline unproven).

entities.name: Newport_Wafer_Fab
entities.notes: UK's largest fab (200mm compound semi). Under the NSI Act 2021 the UK ordered divestment of 86% (Nov 2022) after Nexperia/Wingtech (China-owned) had bought 100%. Sold to US-based Vishay (~$177M, Mar 2024) - forced Chinese exit to allied ownership.

entities.name: Nexperia_Wingtech
entities.notes: Nexperia (Dutch-incorporated, ultimately China-owned via Wingtech). Bought Newport 100% by Jul 2021; ordered to divest 86%; denied national-security concerns. 2025 Dutch government intervention over Wingtech control escalated further.

entities.name: CHIPS_Act
entities.notes: CHIPS & Science Act. Onshoring incentives: Intel (largest awardee), GlobalFoundries (defense/essential chips), TSMC Arizona (leading-edge), Samsung Taylor TX - onshoring the very chokepoint the trusted regime worries about.
